sections.t: What we look for and where
items: Breaches: we check your email against Have I Been Pwned, the reference database of known breaches. We send only the email.
Search engines: we search your name (with your city and occupation, if given) to find profiles, directories and data-selling sites.
AI assistants: we ask Perplexity about you and, when configured, ChatGPT and Gemini, and show you the literal answer.
Public avatar: we check whether your email has a public Gravatar profile with linked accounts.
Writing: an AI (Claude, by Anthropic) organises all that in plain language and extracts signals; the score comes from a fixed, auditable rule, not from the AI.

sections.t: What we keep and for how long
items: Your name, email, city and occupation (if given), the report and the sources' answers.
Without an account: everything is deleted automatically after 30 days.
With an account: kept while you have it; you can delete it any time via Support and everything goes, reports included.
Gmail scanner: only sender, subject and date; we don't store emails or the access, which is revoked when it finishes.
We don't sell or share data with anyone. No ads.
We don't look up other people: only whoever confirms their email.
We don't promise deletion: we show you what's visible and claim on your behalf with the law in hand (Art. 17 GDPR and the authority).
We don't store passwords: you sign in with a one-time code or with Google.
You start at 100 and we subtract: each breach with password −15 (max −45); without password −5 (max −15).
AI knows where you work −10; your city −5; public phone or address −15.
Each public profile the AI attributes to you −3 (max −15); false claims about you in AI −5.
Green 70–100, amber 40–69, red 0–39. The rule is fixed: same data, same score.
Everything is encrypted (HTTPS). Source API keys live only on our server.
Access links and codes expire and are single-use.
Daily database backup and service monitoring.
Servers in the European Union; data controller in Spain (see Legal notice).

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: Rastro shows you what information about you is public online and what AI assistants say about you. To do that we process a small amount of personal data. Here is what, why, for how long, and what rights you have, in plain language.

sections.title: 1. Who is responsible
paragraphs: Data controller: {owner}.
Contact for any privacy question or to exercise your rights: {email}.
Website: {domain}.

sections.title: 2. What data we process
paragraphs: What you type in the form: first name, last name, email address and, optionally, your city.
Optionally, your job or company. It is only used to tell you apart from people with your name.
The date and time you gave consent and verified your email.
Your IP address, stored only as a hash (an irreversible fingerprint) to limit the number of reports per person and prevent abuse. We do not keep the IP in clear text.
The generated report: score, findings, recommended actions and the technical responses from the services consulted, kept so we can review errors.

If you create an account (by verifying your email), we also store your email as the account identifier, your language, the date of your last access and, if you turn on monthly monitoring, the date you turned it on. The erasure letters you generate are stored with their status and dates to keep the deadline calendar.

sections.title: 3. Why, and on what legal basis
paragraphs: Purpose: to generate and show you your exposure report, to send you the verification link by email, and to limit use of the service to prevent abuse.
Legal basis: your consent (Article 6(1)(a) GDPR), which you give by ticking the box in the form and confirm by opening the link we email you. Without that double step we search nothing.
You may only request a report about yourself. Requesting one about someone else breaches these terms.

Monthly monitoring (only if you turn it on): every month we query the same sources again with your data and email you only if something changed. You can turn it off in your account or from the link in the email itself.

Inbox scanner (Pro plan only, and only if you connect it): with your authorisation in Google we read only the sender, subject and date of your emails to infer which services you have accounts with. We don't read content, we store no emails or access keys, and we revoke access when done. We keep only the resulting list of services, which you can delete from your account or by writing to us.

sections.title: 4. Who receives your data
paragraphs: To build the report we query third-party services, sending each only what is strictly necessary:
Have I Been Pwned (United Kingdom): receives your email address to check whether it appears in known breaches.
Brave Search (USA): receives your first and last name and, if given, your city and job or company, to search public results.
Perplexity (USA): receives your first and last name and, if given, your city and job or company, to ask what AI says about you.
Anthropic (USA): receives the results above (not your email) to write the report in plain language.
Gravatar (Automattic, USA): receives a hash (irreversible fingerprint) of your email to check whether a public profile is associated with it.

Google (USA): if you connect your Gmail, Google receives your authorisation and we access your email headers through its API, with the read-only permission you grant and can revoke at any time from your Google account.
We also use providers that host and run the service: Supabase (database), Resend (email delivery) and the web hosting provider. They act as data processors under contract.

Some of these providers are outside the European Economic Area. Transfers rely on Standard Contractual Clauses approved by the European Commission or on the EU-US Data Privacy Framework, depending on the provider.
We do not sell your data or share it with anyone else.

sections.title: 5. How long we keep it
paragraphs: 30 days from when you request the report. After that, the request and the report are automatically deleted from our database.

If you have an account, your reports and letters are kept while the account exists, so you can consult them and follow up. You can ask us to delete the account and everything linked to it by writing to {email}.
The hashes used for rate limiting are renewed every 24 hours.
If you want your report deleted sooner, write to {email} from the same address you used to request it.

sections.title: 6. Your rights
paragraphs: You can access your data, correct it, ask us to delete it, object to the processing, ask us to restrict it, and take it with you (portability). You can also withdraw your consent at any time, without affecting what was done before.
To exercise them, write to {email} stating which right you want to exercise and the email you used to request the report. We will reply within one month.
If you believe we have not handled your request properly, you can lodge a complaint with the Spanish Data Protection Agency (www.aepd.es) or your local supervisory authority.

sections.title: 7. Security
paragraphs: Data travels encrypted (HTTPS) and is stored in a database accessible only to the application server. Verification links are single-use and expire after 24 hours.
No system is infallible. That is why we keep the minimum, for the shortest time possible.

sections.title: 8. What Rastro does not do
paragraphs: Rastro does not delete information from the internet or from AI assistants, and does not promise to. It gives you visibility and tells you what you can do.
The report is based on public sources and on answers from automated systems that can be wrong, especially if your name is common. Data may be missing, or some may refer to another person.

sections.title: 9. Minors
paragraphs: The service is intended for people aged 14 and over. If you are younger, do not use it without your parents' or guardians' permission.

sections.title: 10. Changes
paragraphs: If we change this policy, we will publish the new version on this page with an updated date.

notice.title: Legal notice
notice.intro: Terms of use for Rastro. They are short, because the service is too.

sections.title: 1. Owner
paragraphs: This website ({domain}) is owned by {owner}. Contact: {email}.

sections.title: 2. What the service is
paragraphs: Rastro generates, free of charge, an indicative report on the public information that exists online and in AI assistants about the person requesting it.

sections.title: 3. Terms of use
paragraphs: You may only request reports about yourself. Using the service to obtain information about third parties, to harass, discriminate or make decisions affecting other people is prohibited.
You must provide an email address you own. We verify it is yours before generating anything.
We reserve the right to limit or block use of the service if we detect abuse.

sections.title: 4. Liability
paragraphs: The report is indicative. It is built from public sources and automated systems (search engines, breach databases and AI models) that may contain errors, omissions or data about other people with your name.

We do not guarantee that the report is complete or accurate, and we are not responsible for decisions you make based on it. The recommended actions are general suggestions, not personalized legal or technical advice.
Rastro does not remove third-party information and does not guarantee that you can remove it.

sections.title: 5. Intellectual property
paragraphs: Rastro's design, texts and code belong to its owner. Your report is yours: you may save, share or delete it as you wish.

sections.title: 6. Governing law
paragraphs: These terms are governed by Spanish law. Any dispute will be heard by the courts with jurisdiction under consumer legislation.

aepd.guideTitle: How to file it, step by step
steps: Go to the AEPD electronic office: sedeagpd.gob.es → "Reclamaciones" → "Presentar reclamación".
Identify yourself with a digital certificate, Cl@ve or, if you have neither, the form without certificate (you'll be asked for a copy of your ID).
Claimant: your details. Respondent: the site {host}{contact}.
Under "Hechos" (facts) paste the complaint text from this page.
Attach the letter you sent and proof of sending (screenshot of the sent email or form, with the date).
Save the registration number you get at the end. The AEPD usually replies within weeks; if it admits the complaint, it will require the site to delete your data.
aepd.attach1: Copy of the erasure request sent on {sent}.
aepd.attach2: Proof of sending and date (screenshot of the email or form).
aepd.attach3: If they replied insufficiently, a copy of that reply.

aepdTpl.title: COMPLAINT TO THE SPANISH DATA PROTECTION AGENCY (AEPD)
aepdTpl.respondent: RESPONDENT: the controller of the website {host}{contact}.
aepdTpl.f1: 1. At {url} the respondent publishes personal data concerning me ({what}), without my consent or any other legal basis known to me.
aepdTpl.f2: 2. On {sent} I exercised my right to erasure before the respondent under Article 17 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR), requesting deletion of that data and written confirmation. A copy of the request and proof of sending are attached.
aepdTpl.f3: 3. The one-month period set in Article 12(3) GDPR expired on {deadline} without the respondent acting on the request or replying at all.
aepdTpl.l1: Articles 12, 17, 19 and 21 GDPR; Article 77 GDPR and Articles 15 and 63 et seq. of Spanish Organic Law 3/2018 on Personal Data Protection and digital rights, which recognise the right to lodge a complaint with the supervisory authority when the controller fails to act on a rights request in time.
aepdTpl.r1: That this complaint be admitted and, after the appropriate proceedings, the respondent be required to erase the personal data concerning me and confirm its deletion, without prejudice to any other measures the Agency deems appropriate.
aepdTpl.d1: 1. Copy of the erasure request sent on {sent}.
aepdTpl.f3refused: 3. The respondent replied refusing to comply or imposing undue conditions. A copy of the reply is attached.
aepdTpl.f2b: Given the lack of reply, on {followUp} a reminder of the request was sent.
aepdTpl.d3: 3. Copy of the reminder sent on {followUp}.

extPrivacy.title: Rastro Guardián extension privacy policy
extPrivacy.intro: Rastro Guardián is a browser extension that reviews the cookies of the site you visit and summarizes them in plain language. This policy explains what data it touches and what it doesn't. Short version: everything happens inside your browser and we send nothing to any server.

sections.title: What the extension does
paragraphs: On every page it counts the cookies set by the site and by third-party companies, classifies each one, computes a privacy score from 0 to 100 and shows it on a floating character and on the toolbar icon. It checks whether the domain name imitates a well-known brand (banks, couriers, government) and, if so, warns you and shows the official site. If you ask, it clicks the most private option of the cookie banner for you and blocks advertising trackers.

sections.title: What data it reads
paragraphs: Only cookie metadata: name, domain, expiry and whether they are secure (HttpOnly/Secure). It never reads the value of any cookie. It also looks at the domains of scripts and images loaded by the page to know which companies are present, the domain name you visit and whether the page has a password or card field (only whether it exists; never what you type in it).
It does not read your browsing history, page content or what you type, and it never accesses your passwords or accounts.

sections.title: What data it sends
paragraphs: None. The extension has no connection to any server, not even Rastro's. It uses no analytics, remote logging or user identifiers. Our code verifies this with an automated test that fails if any network call appears.

sections.title: What it stores in your browser
paragraphs: The robot you chose and its position on screen, the list of sites where you clicked “Hide here”, and the summary of the current tab while it is open (cleared when the browser closes). Everything is kept in the extension's local storage on your device and removed when you uninstall it.

sections.title: Permissions and why
paragraphs: “cookies”: to read the metadata of the cookies of the site you visit and count them. “storage”: to remember your preferences. “declarativeNetRequest”: for the optional tracker blocking, with a fixed list bundled in the extension; it is off by default and the browser applies the rules without the extension seeing your traffic. “Access to data on all websites”: to show the robot and analyze any page you open. It does not request history, tabs or downloads.

sections.title: Account and payment
paragraphs: No account or payment is needed. The “View in Rastro” link takes you to rastropro.com if you want to ask a site to remove your data; that step is voluntary and governed by the website's privacy policy.

sections.title: Controller and contact
paragraphs: Controller: {owner}. Contact: {email}. Write to us with any question about the extension or this policy.

sections.title: Changes
paragraphs: If the extension ever needed to send any data (for example for an optional feature), we would say so here and ask for permission first, inside the browser itself.

d3.subject: How we remove your data (and how we verify it)
d3.p1Found: You appear on {n} sites that publish or sell personal data. Each one is legally obliged to remove it if you ask.
d3.p1None: Your report found no sites selling your data. Good news, but they change every month.
d3.p2: With Pro, Rastro sends the letter for you from cartas@rastropro.com, follows up on day 20 if they don't answer and checks the page again every week. When your name stops appearing, we tell you and it is kept as dated evidence.
d3.p3: We don't promise to delete. We promise to measure it: your dashboard shows how much data was removed out of what we found.

d7.subject: One week later: is everything the same?
d7.p1Found: A week ago you appeared on {n} data-selling sites. If you haven't requested removal, they're still there.
d7.p1None: A week ago your score was fine. What changes over time are new breaches and what AI learns about you.
d7.p2: Pro watches every month, sends the letters for you and keeps what each AI says about you to alert you if it changes.

d7.price: It costs {monthly} a month or {yearly} a year, cancel anytime.
